question: Select the correct version of the sentence: 'She don't know the answer to the question.'
options: A) She doesn't know the answer to the question.
B) She didn't knew the answer to the question.
C) She not know the answer to the question.
D) She doesn't knew the answer to the question.
correct_answer: A) She doesn't know the answer to the question.
explanation: With third-person singular subjects (she/he/it), we use 'doesn't' + base verb. 'Don't' is used with I/you/we/they. So 'doesn't know' is correct.

question: Choose the grammatically correct sentence: 'He go to school every day.'
options: A) He goes to school every day.
B) He going to school every day.
C) He gone to school every day.
D) He goed to school every day.
correct_answer: A) He goes to school every day.
explanation: In simple present tense, third-person singular subjects require the verb to take an '-s' or '-es' ending. 'He goes' is the correct form.

question: Identify the correct sentence: 'The team are playing well today.'
options: A) The team is playing well today.
B) The team were playing well today.
C) The team have playing well today.
D) The team be playing well today.
correct_answer: A) The team is playing well today.
explanation: Collective nouns like 'team' are treated as singular in American English and take singular verbs. 'The team is' is correct.

question: Find the error and correct: 'I have went to the market yesterday.'
options: A) I went to the market yesterday.
B) I have go to the market yesterday.
C) I had went to the market yesterday.
D) I was went to the market yesterday.
correct_answer: A) I went to the market yesterday.
explanation: With a specific past time reference like 'yesterday', simple past tense is used. 'I went' is correct; present perfect cannot be used with definite past time expressions.

question: Choose the correct sentence: 'Neither of the students have submitted their assignment.'
options: A) Neither of the students has submitted his assignment.
B) Neither of the students have submitted his assignment.
C) Neither of the students has submitted their assignment.
D) Neither of the students had submitted their assignment.
correct_answer: A) Neither of the students has submitted his assignment.
explanation: 'Neither' is singular and takes a singular verb 'has'. The pronoun should also be singular 'his/her'. Option A is the most grammatically precise.

question: Correct the sentence: 'She is more smarter than her brother.'
options: A) She is smarter than her brother.
B) She is more smart than her brother.
C) She is most smarter than her brother.
D) She is smartest than her brother.
correct_answer: A) She is smarter than her brother.
explanation: Double comparatives are incorrect. 'Smarter' is already the comparative form of 'smart', so 'more' should not be added. 'She is smarter' is correct.

question: Select the correct sentence: 'The news are very shocking.'
options: A) The news is very shocking.
B) The news were very shocking.
C) The news have been very shocking.
D) The news are shocking very much.
correct_answer: A) The news is very shocking.
explanation: 'News' is an uncountable noun and always takes a singular verb. 'The news is' is the correct form.

question: Find the correct version: 'He has been working here since three years.'
options: A) He has been working here for three years.
B) He has been working here since three years ago.
C) He had been working here since three years.
D) He was working here for three years.
correct_answer: A) He has been working here for three years.
explanation: 'Since' is used with a point in time (since 2020), while 'for' is used with a duration (for three years). The correct preposition here is 'for'.

question: Choose the grammatically correct option: 'Each of the boys were given a prize.'
options: A) Each of the boys was given a prize.
B) Each of the boys have been given a prize.
C) Each of the boys are given a prize.
D) Each of the boys were giving a prize.
correct_answer: A) Each of the boys was given a prize.
explanation: 'Each' is always singular and takes a singular verb. 'Each of the boys was' is the correct form.

question: Identify the error: 'She laid down on the bed and slept.'
options: A) She lay down on the bed and slept.
B) She lied down on the bed and slept.
C) She lain down on the bed and slept.
D) She laying down on the bed and slept.
correct_answer: A) She lay down on the bed and slept.
explanation: The past tense of 'lie' (to recline) is 'lay'. 'Laid' is the past tense of 'lay' (to place something). So 'she lay down' is correct.

question: Correct the sentence: 'The furniture's are very expensive.'
options: A) The furniture is very expensive.
B) The furnitures are very expensive.
C) The furniture are very expensive.
D) The furnitures is very expensive.
correct_answer: A) The furniture is very expensive.
explanation: 'Furniture' is an uncountable noun; it has no plural form and takes a singular verb. 'The furniture is' is correct.

question: Select the correct sentence: 'He is one of the student who has passed.'
options: A) He is one of the students who have passed.
B) He is one of the students who has passed.
C) He is one of the student who have passed.
D) He is one of the students who had passed.
correct_answer: A) He is one of the students who have passed.
explanation: In 'one of the students who...', the relative clause refers to 'students' (plural), so the verb should be 'have'. 'One of the students who have passed' is correct.

question: Find the correct version: 'I am knowing the answer.'
options: A) I know the answer.
B) I am known the answer.
C) I have been knowing the answer.
D) I was knowing the answer.
correct_answer: A) I know the answer.
explanation: 'Know' is a stative verb and cannot be used in continuous tenses. Simple present 'I know' is the correct form.

question: Choose the correct sentence: 'He told me that he will come tomorrow.'
options: A) He told me that he would come the next day.
B) He told me that he will come the next day.
C) He told me that he shall come tomorrow.
D) He told me that he comes tomorrow.
correct_answer: A) He told me that he would come the next day.
explanation: In reported speech, 'will' changes to 'would' and 'tomorrow' changes to 'the next day' when the reporting verb is in past tense.

question: Correct the sentence: 'Between you and I, this is a secret.'
options: A) Between you and me, this is a secret.
B) Between you and myself, this is a secret.
C) Among you and me, this is a secret.
D) Between you and I, this is a secret.
correct_answer: A) Between you and me, this is a secret.
explanation: Prepositions like 'between' are followed by object pronouns. 'Me' is the object form of 'I', so 'between you and me' is correct.

question: Identify the correct sentence: 'The police has arrested the thief.'
options: A) The police have arrested the thief.
B) The police has been arrested the thief.
C) The police is arresting the thief yesterday.
D) The police were arresting the thief.
correct_answer: A) The police have arrested the thief.
explanation: 'Police' is a plural noun and always takes a plural verb. 'The police have' is the correct form.

question: Select the correct version: 'She is elder than her sister.'
options: A) She is older than her sister.
B) She is eldest than her sister.
C) She is more elder than her sister.
D) She is the elder than her sister.
correct_answer: A) She is older than her sister.
explanation: 'Elder' is not used with 'than' in comparisons. 'Older than' is the correct comparative form when comparing ages.

question: Correct the sentence: 'He could not help but to laugh.'
options: A) He could not help laughing.
B) He could not help but laughing.
C) He could not help to laugh.
D) He could not help but laugh at.
correct_answer: A) He could not help laughing.
explanation: The idiom 'cannot help' is followed by a gerund (-ing form). 'He could not help laughing' is the correct structure.

question: Find the error: 'The scissors is on the table.'
options: A) The scissors are on the table.
B) The scissor is on the table.
C) The scissors was on the table.
D) The scissors has been on the table.
correct_answer: A) The scissors are on the table.
explanation: 'Scissors' is a plural noun (always used in plural form) and takes a plural verb. 'The scissors are' is correct.

question: Choose the correct sentence: 'I have seen him yesterday.'
options: A) I saw him yesterday.
B) I have saw him yesterday.
C) I had seen him yesterday.
D) I was seeing him yesterday.
correct_answer: A) I saw him yesterday.
explanation: Present perfect cannot be used with specific past time expressions like 'yesterday'. Simple past 'I saw' is correct.

question: Correct the sentence: 'She is more prettier than her friend.'
options: A) She is prettier than her friend.
B) She is more pretty than her friend.
C) She is prettiest than her friend.
D) She is most prettier than her friend.
correct_answer: A) She is prettier than her friend.
explanation: Double comparatives are incorrect. 'Prettier' is already the comparative form of 'pretty', so 'more' should not be added.

question: Identify the correct sentence: 'He is working in this company since 2018.'
options: A) He has been working in this company since 2018.
B) He is working in this company for 2018.
C) He was working in this company since 2018.
D) He had been working in this company since 2018.
correct_answer: A) He has been working in this company since 2018.
explanation: For an action that started in the past and continues to the present, present perfect continuous is used with 'since' + point in time.

question: Select the correct version: 'The boy as well as his friends are going.'
options: A) The boy as well as his friends is going.
B) The boy as well as his friends were going.
C) The boy as well as his friends have gone.
D) The boy as well as his friends are going.
correct_answer: A) The boy as well as his friends is going.
explanation: When 'as well as' connects two subjects, the verb agrees with the first subject. 'The boy' is singular, so 'is going' is correct.

question: Correct the sentence: 'I prefer tea over coffee.'
options: A) I prefer tea to coffee.
B) I prefer tea than coffee.
C) I prefer tea above coffee.
D) I prefer tea from coffee.
correct_answer: A) I prefer tea to coffee.
explanation: The verb 'prefer' is followed by 'to', not 'over', 'than', or 'above'. 'I prefer tea to coffee' is the correct structure.

question: Find the correct sentence: 'He is too weak that he cannot walk.'
options: A) He is too weak to walk.
B) He is so weak that he cannot walk.
C) He is very weak that he cannot walk.
D) Both A and B are correct.
correct_answer: D) Both A and B are correct.
explanation: 'Too...to' and 'so...that' are both correct structures. 'Too weak to walk' and 'so weak that he cannot walk' are both grammatically correct.

question: Choose the correct sentence: 'Neither Ram nor his brothers was present.'
options: A) Neither Ram nor his brothers were present.
B) Neither Ram nor his brothers has been present.
C) Neither Ram nor his brothers is present.
D) Neither Ram nor his brothers are been present.
correct_answer: A) Neither Ram nor his brothers were present.
explanation: With 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the subject closest to it. 'Brothers' is plural, so 'were' is correct.

question: Identify the error: 'He has a lot of informations about the topic.'
options: A) He has a lot of information about the topic.
B) He has a lot of informations on the topic.
C) He has many informations about the topic.
D) He has much informations about the topic.
correct_answer: A) He has a lot of information about the topic.
explanation: 'Information' is an uncountable noun and has no plural form. 'A lot of information' is the correct usage.

question: Select the correct version: 'She suggested me to take rest.'
options: A) She suggested that I should take rest.
B) She suggested me taking rest.
C) She suggested to me to take rest.
D) She suggested me for taking rest.
correct_answer: A) She suggested that I should take rest.
explanation: 'Suggest' cannot be followed by an object + infinitive. The correct structure is 'suggest + that clause' or 'suggest + gerund'.

question: Correct the sentence: 'The number of students are increasing.'
options: A) The number of students is increasing.
B) The number of students were increasing.
C) A number of students is increasing.
D) The number of students have increased.
correct_answer: A) The number of students is increasing.
explanation: 'The number of' takes a singular verb, while 'a number of' takes a plural verb. 'The number of students is' is correct.

question: Find the correct sentence: 'He is good in mathematics.'
options: A) He is good at mathematics.
B) He is good with mathematics.
C) He is good for mathematics.
D) He is good on mathematics.
correct_answer: A) He is good at mathematics.
explanation: The correct preposition after 'good' when referring to a skill or subject is 'at'. 'Good at mathematics' is the correct phrase.

question: Choose the correct sentence: 'She has many luggages with her.'
options: A) She has a lot of luggage with her.
B) She has many luggage with her.
C) She has much luggages with her.
D) She has several luggages with her.
correct_answer: A) She has a lot of luggage with her.
explanation: 'Luggage' is an uncountable noun and cannot be pluralized. 'A lot of luggage' is the correct expression.

question: Identify the correct sentence: 'He is married with a doctor.'
options: A) He is married to a doctor.
B) He is married with doctor.
C) He is married by a doctor.
D) He is married for a doctor.
correct_answer: A) He is married to a doctor.
explanation: The correct preposition after 'married' is 'to'. 'Married to' is the standard English expression.

question: Correct the sentence: 'I am having a headache.'
options: A) I have a headache.
B) I am having headache.
C) I have been having a headache.
D) I had been having a headache.
correct_answer: A) I have a headache.
explanation: 'Have' when used to express possession or a state (like having a headache) is a stative verb and cannot be used in continuous form.

question: Select the correct version: 'The teacher, along with students, are going on a trip.'
options: A) The teacher, along with students, is going on a trip.
B) The teacher, along with students, were going on a trip.
C) The teacher, along with students, have gone on a trip.
D) The teacher, along with students, are going on a trip.
correct_answer: A) The teacher, along with students, is going on a trip.
explanation: When 'along with' connects two subjects, the verb agrees with the first subject. 'The teacher' is singular, so 'is going' is correct.

question: Find the error: 'She is looking forward to meet you.'
options: A) She is looking forward to meeting you.
B) She is looking forward to met you.
C) She is looking forward for meeting you.
D) She is looking forward to have met you.
correct_answer: A) She is looking forward to meeting you.
explanation: In 'look forward to', the 'to' is a preposition, not part of an infinitive. It must be followed by a gerund (-ing form).

question: Choose the correct sentence: 'He denied to have stolen the money.'
options: A) He denied having stolen the money.
B) He denied to steal the money.
C) He denied for stealing the money.
D) He denied that he stole the money.
correct_answer: A) He denied having stolen the money.
explanation: 'Deny' is followed by a gerund, not an infinitive. 'Denied having stolen' is the correct structure.

question: Identify the correct sentence: 'He is used to work late at night.'
options: A) He is used to working late at night.
B) He is used to worked late at night.
C) He used to working late at night.
D) He is use to work late at night.
correct_answer: A) He is used to working late at night.
explanation: 'Be used to' means 'be accustomed to' and is followed by a gerund. 'Is used to working' is correct.

question: Correct the sentence: 'She has less friends than I expected.'
options: A) She has fewer friends than I expected.
B) She has lesser friends than I expected.
C) She has less friend than I expected.
D) She has fewest friends than I expected.
correct_answer: A) She has fewer friends than I expected.
explanation: 'Fewer' is used with countable nouns (friends), while 'less' is used with uncountable nouns. 'Fewer friends' is correct.

question: Select the correct version: 'He is the most tallest player in the team.'
options: A) He is the tallest player in the team.
B) He is the most tall player in the team.
C) He is the more tallest player in the team.
D) He is the taller player in the team.
correct_answer: A) He is the tallest player in the team.
explanation: Double superlatives are incorrect. 'Tallest' is already the superlative form of 'tall', so 'most' should not be added.

question: Find the correct sentence: 'I am tired. I want to lay down.'
options: A) I am tired. I want to lie down.
B) I am tired. I want to laid down.
C) I am tired. I want to lain down.
D) I am tired. I want to lying down.
correct_answer: A) I am tired. I want to lie down.
explanation: 'Lie down' means to recline. The infinitive form is 'to lie'. 'Lay' means to place something, which is incorrect here.

question: Choose the correct sentence: 'The committee have decided to postpone the meeting.'
options: A) The committee has decided to postpone the meeting.
B) The committee had decided to postpone the meeting.
C) The committee have been decided to postpone the meeting.
D) The committee decides to postpone the meeting.
correct_answer: A) The committee has decided to postpone the meeting.
explanation: In formal/American English, collective nouns like 'committee' take singular verbs. 'The committee has decided' is correct.

question: Identify the error: 'No sooner did he arrive than the meeting was started.'
options: A) No sooner did he arrive than the meeting started.
B) No sooner had he arrived than the meeting started.
C) No sooner he arrived than the meeting started.
D) No sooner did he arrive when the meeting started.
correct_answer: B) No sooner had he arrived than the meeting started.
explanation: 'No sooner...than' uses past perfect in the first clause. 'No sooner had he arrived than the meeting started' is the correct structure.

question: Select the correct version: 'Scarcely had she left when he arrived.'
options: A) Scarcely had she left when he arrived.
B) Scarcely she had left when he arrived.
C) Scarcely had she left than he arrived.
D) Scarcely did she leave when he arrived.
correct_answer: A) Scarcely had she left when he arrived.
explanation: 'Scarcely...when' is the correct correlative conjunction pair. The sentence is already correct as given in option A.

question: Correct the sentence: 'He is one of those men who believes in hard work.'
options: A) He is one of those men who believe in hard work.
B) He is one of those men who has believed in hard work.
C) He is one of those men who is believing in hard work.
D) He is one of those men who believed in hard work.
correct_answer: A) He is one of those men who believe in hard work.
explanation: The relative clause 'who believe' refers to 'those men' (plural), so the verb must be plural 'believe'.

question: Find the correct sentence: 'The data shows that crime rates are falling.'
options: A) The data show that crime rates are falling.
B) The data is showing that crime rates are falling.
C) The data shows that crime rates are falling.
D) The data were showing that crime rates are falling.
correct_answer: A) The data show that crime rates are falling.
explanation: 'Data' is the plural of 'datum' and traditionally takes a plural verb in formal writing. 'The data show' is grammatically correct.
